input.command:
cd /home/nab-raj.roshyara@dg-nexolution.de/roshyara/personal/nrna1/docs/knowledgeos/knowlegeos_manual_theory_20261018/06-theory/manuscript; python3 -I - <<'EOF'
p='chapter_01/CH-01-knowledge-authority-execution.md'; s=open(p).read()
R=[
# F1, F18
("**A census of realization levels (Src, observed; SI L206–231; verified in part; added R1-11).** An inventory of the platform's own mechanisms grades how each of 20 recorded contracts is actually held:",
 "**A census of enforcement modes (Src: SI L206–231, graded OBSERVED by SI except K-14 and K-15, which SI grades INFERRED; added R1-11, corrected after the batch review).** An inventory of the platform's own mechanisms records **how** each of 20 contracts is enforced. This is a census of **enforcement mode**, not of realization level: Ch. 2 §2.9 keeps the two apart (an executable check can still be advisory). The counts:"),
("- **checked by a gate, threshold, error, enumeration, structural rule or fail-closed guard**: 8;",
 "- **checked by a gate, threshold, error, enumeration, structural rule, fail-closed guard, or an \"exit 2 = unruled\" result**: 8;"),
# F3, F2, F12
("It is realized by a type restriction: the verdict enumeration lets a mechanism emit only PASS, FAIL, WARN and INCONCLUSIVE. The values reserved for review acts are excluded by `Verdict::emittable()` (**verified by reading the code**: `scripts/lib/EngineeringKnowledge/Shared/Domain/Verdict.php` L31–33; not tested by execution). *What this establishes, and what it does not:* it guarantees **one boundary** of the invariant, namely that a verdict-emitting mechanism of this library cannot output a review-act verdict. It does **not** establish the whole invariant. Other mechanisms can still produce the effects of authority, e.g. a gate switched to blocking by configuration (§1.14.5). *Reading (Ded):* this is the realization ladder measured. **Most contracts sit low on it**, and the one principle at its top is the one this book treats as the core authority rule. The same inventory confirms the two verdict vocabularies noted above: `AssessmentService` uses SUPPORTED · PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED · NOT_SUPPORTED · INCONCLUSIVE (**verified**, `scripts/observations/AssessmentService.php` L10–41). The scale for partial support is therefore already in use while the governed verdict vocabulary lacks it (open question OQ-28 of the sources).",
 "*What \"compiled\" amounts to (verified by reading the code, not by execution).* The verdict enumeration declares all seven values. `Verdict::emittable()` is a list of the four values a mechanism may emit (`Verdict.php` L31–33), and the actual enforcement is a **runtime exception** when an `Assessment` is created with a reserved value (`Assessment.php` L38–42). So it is **one runtime guard on one code path**: an `Assessment` object cannot carry a review-act verdict. It is **not** a compile-time guarantee, and it does **not** establish the invariant \"knowledge feeds authority, never holds it\" in general. Other code can reference reserved values directly, other vocabularies are unconstrained, and other mechanisms can produce the effects of authority (e.g. a gate switched to blocking by configuration, §1.14.5). *Reading (Int):* 11 of the 20 contracts are enforced by something stronger than advice or convention; 9 rely on advice or convention. *Two facts about verdict vocabularies, stated as facts only:* `AssessmentService` emits SUPPORTED · PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED · NOT_SUPPORTED · INCONCLUSIVE as plain strings (`AssessmentService.php` L10–41), and a source proposes a third vocabulary with UNKNOWN and REFUTED [PC L175]. Whether the governed verdict vocabulary should admit partial support (OQ-28) is not decided by either fact. Decision B above keeps vocabularies of different kinds apart."),
# F17
("*Reading (Ded):* every one is a **self-report diverging from behaviour**, the case this section describes, found in the platform's own enforcement.",
 "*Reading (Ded):* in each case a **declaration diverged from behaviour**: a printed message, a declared hook wiring (incident 3 produced no report at all; the divergence was between the wiring declaration and what ran), a header, or a registry entry. That is the case this section describes, found in the platform's own enforcement."),
("The inventory notes that the cure is applied only to some gates [SI L273].",
 "The inventory notes that the cure is applied only to some gates [SI L273]. *A limit of the cure (verified, `scripts/design-check.sh` L42–46):* the design gate fills **missing** settings with hard-coded defaults (e.g. threshold 150, `exit_on_fail` false). An absent policy value is therefore silently replaced by a specified one, the failure Ch. 2 §2.8.8 names (\"E2 silently replaced by a specified value\"). The guard catches unreadable values, not missing ones."),
# F6
("- **duplicate ownership**: one invariant (domain-layer purity) enforced by a blocking gate and by an advisory reminder that do not reference each other, with \"no contract stating which is authoritative\" [SI L300]. That is the P-7 failure;",
 "- **potential duplicate ownership** [SI L300]: domain-layer purity is checked by a blocking gate and touched by an advisory reminder that do not reference each other, with \"no contract stating which is authoritative\". Two readings: (i) one invariant with two owners, the P-7 failure; (ii) the inventory itself lists them under **different contracts** (K-11 domain purity; K-6 the seven DDD principles, of which purity is one), so they **overlap** rather than duplicate [SI L215, L220];"),
# F11
("The source proposes a narrower version of this as a new invariant (its OQ-33: \"not a value produced during the activating transaction\").",
 "*This differs from the source, and the difference is a trade-off (two concepts, kept):* the source forbids an approval reference that is \"a value produced during the activating transaction\" (its OQ-33) [DE L301]. That rule can be **checked by machine** from transaction boundaries, but it excludes a human approval recorded atomically with its effect. The book's condition allows that case, but relies on **recorded authorship**, which ultimately rests on the trust assumption of §1.12. Neither is a narrower version of the other."),
("This is §1.14.1's \"derived, never stored\" (I-9), reached independently.",
 "This is §1.14.1's point that current authority is derived and never stored, reached independently."),
# F14
("**The list omits the anchor:** the **record of the human act itself** and the **grant** under which it was made (§1.13). In this theory every standing transition must point to one (§1.6), so it is a sixth kind of record, and the only one that is *not* produced by the system.",
 "**AB's five-item list omits the anchor:** the **record of the human act itself** and the **grant** under which it was made (§1.13). In this theory every standing transition must point to one (§1.6), so it is a sixth kind of record. It is the only one whose **act** is not produced by the system; its record, like all records, is (§1.12)."),
("| **audit event** | an accountability record: actor, policy version, provenance |",
 "| **audit event** | an accountability record: actor, policy version, request identity, provenance, integrity protection [DE L85] |"),
# F20
("*Analysis (Ded):* the rule above bounds a derived item's visibility by its **sources**.",
 "*Analysis (Ded):* the example covers **two cases**. (i) A **stored** restricted edge between two visible nodes: this is incomplete lineage, and the intersection bound handles it if the edge itself is counted among the sources. (ii) An **inferred** edge, computed from visible items only: the aggregation case. The rule above bounds a derived item's visibility by its **sources**."),
# F19
("So ranking by similarity can only follow filtering by visibility, applicability and standing, never replace it.)",
 "So similarity ranking can never **replace** filtering by visibility, applicability and standing. Filtering must have happened **before the result is used**, whatever the order of computation.)"),
]
for a,b in R:
    assert s.count(a)==1,a[:60]; s=s.replace(a,b)
open(p,'w').write(s); print('ok')
EOF
